questions.q: Why must Accounts be loaded before Contacts in a typical migration?
options: Contacts cannot be loaded at all in Data Loader
Salesforce loads objects in alphabetical order only
Each Contact links to an Account, and the parent record must exist before the child can reference it
Accounts are smaller, so they load faster
questions.explain: Children reference parents, so parents must be loaded first.

questions.q: What is an External Id field used for in a migration?
options: Holding the source system's key on the Salesforce record, so records can be matched or linked without knowing new Salesforce Ids
Hiding a record from other users
Encrypting the record's Id
Replacing the Salesforce Id permanently
questions.explain: An External Id stores the legacy key, allowing upsert matching and parent linking through the relationship.

questions.q: How can a Contact row reference its parent Account when you don't know the new Account's Salesforce Id?
options: By leaving the parent blank and fixing it manually later
By using the Contact's own Id as the Account Id
It cannot be done
By mapping the parent relationship to the Account's External Id field (for example Account:Legacy_Id__c)
questions.explain: Data Loader can resolve the parent through its External Id field via the relationship.

questions.q: Why does an upsert on an External Id make a migration rerun safer?
options: It deletes every existing record first
Records that already exist are updated instead of being created again as duplicates
It skips validation rules
It changes all Ids to 15 characters
questions.explain: Upsert matches on the External Id, inserting new rows and updating existing ones.

questions.q: Which lookup usually needs a second load pass?
options: The Name field on Account
The Phone field on Contact
A self-referencing lookup such as an Account's Parent Account, since the parent must exist first
The Description field on Opportunity
questions.explain: When an object references itself, load the records first and then update the lookup in a second pass.
